newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends near one year highs.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends near one year highs.

text.p: COMEX copper ended near one year highs Thursday as the London market broke through key chart areas, triggering speculative buying and shortcovering amid falling stocks, good demand and labor concerns at key mines, dealers said.
Tags have now recovered to their pre-Sumitomo highs, defying many analysts who had expected prices to continue sliding slowly as anticipated fresh production was due to hit the market.
LME stocks fell 3,225 tonnes Thursday to 146,075 tonnes.
Overnight gains on LME where the three months contract broke through $2,445 per tonne, spilled over into COMEX where there was also good buying, dealers said.
"This triggered a fresh wave of speculative buying when we got above that old high," Fred Demler of E D and F Man International said.
July COMEX copper settled 2.60 cents firmer at 116.40 cents per pound, traded 117.10 to 114.90 cents. Spot March went out 3.00 cents higher at 117.00 cents.
The push upwards was fueled by an overnight doubling of the LME cash to three months backwardation, easing slightly by COMEX close to $95/$105.

Meanwhile Chilean state copper workers will consider calling a strike action to protest the government's reported plans to privatize parts of state metals smelting firm Enami and state oil company Enap, union leaders said on Thursday.
In addition, unions representing some 700 supervisors at Chile's huge, state-owned Chuquicamata copper mine are in talks to renew a pay deal which expires at the end of May.
The supervisors will vote May 27 whether to accept the government's offer or strike in early June.
